text:
maria: heads up — starting ~10:15 UTC a bunch of training jobs in us-west-2 are stuck in Pending. Dashboard shows GPUs 'Available' but pods not scheduling. Anyone else?
aj: seeing that too. node-exporter shows normal alloc, kube-scheduler logs show binds failing with endpoint lookup timeouts.
samir: can you share a pod that's pending? run `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl get endpoints -n training` for the headless services.
maria: pasted `kubectl describe` -> Events: FailedScheduling: 0/24 nodes are available: 24 network plugin denied.
ops-sre: "network plugin denied" screams NetworkPolicy. Did any netpols land in the last deploy window?
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: `infra/tenant-onboard` applied 1768001100 by ci-user — created networkpolicy `deny-external-egress` in namespaces matching label tenant=thirdparty.
aj: pinged the CI job owner, they pushed a podSelector-based egress allowlist intended to restrict external calls, but it looks like it omitted intra-namespace and cross-namespace headless service CIDRs.
maria: here's `kubectl get networkpolicy -n training deny-external-egress -o yaml` snippet:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-external-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 34.210.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
samir: omg it's a blanket podSelector with only a specific external CIDR allowed — that forbids any egress to cluster CIDRs (10.42.0.0/16) and overlay CIDRs (vxlan 10.244.0.0/16). Headless services are cluster-internal.
ops-sre: confirmed with `tcpdump` on node: repeated SYN retransmits to headless svc IPs and then conntrack entries show short TTLs. Example from node0:
```
16:18:20.123456 IP 10.42.5.12.34567 > 10.244.12.34.30421: Flags [S], seq 0
16:18:20.523789 IP 10.42.5.12.34567 > 10.244.12.34.30421: Flags [S], seq 0 (retry)
```
maria: also seeing `vxlan` fragmentation warnings in dmesg — MTU mismatch because nodes use ipip/encap for calico and the egress policy blocked the path causing packets to traverse unexpected logical path and exceed MTU.
aj: interesting — so netpol blocked endpoint egress, forcing pod -> host route changes? maybe kube-proxy stun?
samir: more likely: when netpol denies egress to the pod, the CNI handles rejected flows by dropping; but some flows (probe/tcp handshake) retried and created conntrack state. Once conntrack fills, unrelated services get symptoms.
devex: this explains why GPUs show available — kubelet and device-plugin happy, but application-level handshakes to parameter servers fail so the scheduler marks jobs Pending.
ops-sre: temporary mitigation: add an egress rule to allow cluster CIDR and kube-system namespaces. Run:
```
kubectl patch networkpolicy deny-external-egress -n training --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/egress/0/to/-","value":{"ipBlock":{"cidr":"10.0.0.0/8"}}}]'
```
aj: patched, and I also added a rule to allow pods -> namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: role=kube-system} for DNS/kube-proxy.
maria: after patch, pending pods started scheduling within ~30s. Jobs resumed. Thanks.
ops-sre: root cause: onboarding automation used podSelector-scoped deny with a single external ipBlock allow — too narrow. It blocked intra-cluster service traffic and VXLAN encapsulated packets, exacerbating MTU fragmentation and conntrack churn.
samir: action items: 1) revert onboarding CI to create default egress allowing clusterCIDR+kube-system. 2) add lint to infra-policies repo to forbid bare podSelector-only deny egress without explicit cluster CIDR allow. 3) add a Canary job to exercise headless svc flows post-policy.
devex: I'll draft the policy-lint rule. Proposed regexp: disallow spec.policyTypes contains Egress + podSelector exists + egress allows only ipBlock not matching cluster CIDR.
aj: also adding a monitoring alert: "pod netpol egress denied" events spike -> page ops-sre.
ops-sre: leaving notes in runbook: how to quickly identify with `kubectl get netpol -A --field-selector metadata.name=deny-external-egress` and `tcpdump -n -i any host <svc-ip>` and patch command above.
maria: thanks all — putting a postmortem in /incidents and tagging infra on the CI change. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: linked ticket INF-4921 created for policy lint and canary tests."
